data.content_ref: inline:The target claims that the cross-city modulation of the nocturnal UHI gap 'scales with city size and wind speed,' predicting the gap is more pronounced 'under conditions that would otherwise maximize rural stability' (i.e., very calm winds). However, this is internally contradictory with its stated single mechanism of reduced turbulent sensible heat transport. The mechanism requires wind shear to generate urban turbulence; under the very low-wind conditions that maximize rural stability (and thus the baseline temperature gap), urban turbulence also collapses. This is even conceded in the target's own counterconditions ("If wind speed is very low, urban turbulence may also collapse, reducing the difference in boundary layer depth"). Consequently, wind speed cannot monotonically scale the gap upward under the proposed mechanism, and the target fails to coherently explain why the night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others.
